thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Climbs More Than 190 Points, But Tech And Internet-related Stocks Sink Nasdaq

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Climbs More Than 190 Points, But Tech And Internet-related Stocks Sink Nasdaq
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch , Chris Matthews
Apple's stock decline weighs on broader market
U.S. stocks logged a mixed performance during trading Monday, ahead of an updated policy statement from the Federal Reserve and midterm elections that could alter the balance of power in Washington.
How did benchmarks fare?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 190.87 points to 25,461.70, a gain of 0.8%, and the S&P 500 added 15.25 points, or 0.6%, to end at 2,738.31. The Nasdaq Composite Index , meanwhile, fell 28.14 points, or 0.4%, to 7,328.85.
Last week, both the Dow and the S&P 500 rose 2.4% and the Nasdaq advanced 2.7%, its first weekly gain since the end of September.
What drove the market?
Midterm congressional elections, which are expected to see Democrats take control of the House and Republicans maintain a grip on the Senate, take place Tuesday. On Thursday, the Fed concludes a two-day policy meeting, which isn't expected to deliver a change in rates, but may offer fresh insights to investors about the pace of coming rate increases and the effects of trade clashes between the U.S. and China on the domestic economy.
On Monday, China's President Xi Jinping, speaking at a trade expo in Shangha (https://www.bbc.com/news/business-46093478)i, vowed to address criticisms that its trade practices are "unfair," by reducing its tariffs and opening up its economy to more imports.
On Friday, markets contended with a series of conflicting headlines on the progress of negotiations between Beijing and Washington. Stocks pared losses in late trade (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-cuts-intraday-loss-after-trump-declares-progress-on-trade-deal-with-china-directly-countering-kudlow-2018-11-02) Friday after President Donald Trump said progress was being made in talks with Chinese leadership. A few hours earlier, his top economic adviser, Larry Kudlow, said the U.S. and China were a long way from reaching a trade deal.
Read:How U.S.-China trade talks are the biggest catalyst for the stock market (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-chart-shows-why-trade-war-fears-are-the-biggest-catalyst-for-the-stock-market-2018-11-02)
Which stocks are in focus?
Shares of Apple Inc.(AAPL) fell 2.8% following the iPhone maker's 6.6% stock decline on Friday, after saying it would no longer disclose (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/when-the-going-gets-tough-apple-hides-its-numbers-2018-11-01) unit sales of its products for investors, as it has for more than a decade. Market participants also reacted to reports that Apple demand for its XR phones may be falling short of expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-stock-on-track-for-worst-two-day-stretch-in-nearly-six-years-amid-iphone-xr-concerns-2018-11-05).
Under Armour Inc. (UAA) stock rose 1.2%, after analysts at Stifel Nicolaus upgraded their price target for the firm to $30, from $27.
Shares of Sysco Corp. (SYY) fell 9.4% Monday, after the company missed earnings estimates (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sysco-shares-slide-6-premarket-after-earnings-miss-2018-11-05) for the first fiscal quarter of 2019. The stock is on pace for largest percent decrease since Black Monday, Oct. 19, 1987, when it fell 25.86%, according to Dow Jones Market Data.
Cabot Oil & Gas Corp., (COG) jumped 5.9% and EQT Corp. advanced more than 8.3% as natural-gas prices rose sharply on forecasts turning toward colder weather then previously expected (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-bounce-around-as-iran-sanctions-kick-in-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-bounce-around-as-iran-sanctions-kick-in-2018-11-05)across much of the U.S. later this month. December natural-gas futures surged 8.3% and hit a nine-month high.
Shares of home-improvement retailer Lowe's Companies(LOW) rose 0.3% after the company said it would close 20 underperforming stored in the U.S. and 31 stores in Canada (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/lowes-to-close-51-stores-including-20-in-the-us-2018-11-05) as part of a strategic reassessment.
Activision Blizzard (ATVI)shares tumbled 6.7%, ahead of the company's third-quarter earnings announcement on Thursday.
Shares of Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) were in focus after reports that the retailing giant was set to pick two cities to host its second headquarters. Shares of Amazon slipped 2.3% Monday.
Read:These Lowe's stores are closing in the next three months (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/these-lowes-stores-are-closing-in-the-next-three-months-2018-11-05)
What data are in focus
The Markit services industry index came in at 54.8 for October, versus expectations of 54.7, according to FactSet.
The ISM services index slipped to 60.3 in October (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-economy-still-running-strong-in-october-ism-services-survey-shows-2018-11-05), down from 61.6 in September, but beating the 58.6 average estimate of economists surveyed by MarketWatch.
What are analysts saying?
"You're seeing a rotation out of FANG stocks, plus Apple, and into the rest of the market," Michael O'Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading told MarketWatch, using the acronym popularly applied to the tech companies Facebook (FB),Amazon (AMZN),Netflix(NFLX)and Google parentAlphabet(GOOGL), which have powered much of the market gains this year and in 2017.
"Google is the only one of these companies not to have some sort of stumble" in recent quarters O'Rourke said, adding that investors have begun to re-evaluate their estimates of future profit growth for these big-name tech firms.
"Investors face a wall of worry," that must be climbed for stocks to recapture their September highs, Peter Bye, portfolio manager at UBS Asset Management told MarketWatch. Bye said that slowing growth in China and Europe, combined with rising interest rates at home, are making traders nervous about how much longer the current economic expansion can last.
"You've got increasing evidence of pressure on tech leaders," like Google and Facebook, which investors have counted on to power the bull market, Bye warned. "They are facing multiple, new headwinds," like new digital taxes abroad (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tech-giants-face-global-push-for-digital-taxes-2018-10-28) to bipartisan interest in regulating the U.S. tech industry, he said.
How are other markets trading?
Asian stock markets ended down across the board (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-fall-on-profit-taking-while-xi-praises-globalization-2018-11-04) Monday, while the main pan-European stock index (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-struggle-against-backdrop-of-sluggish-global-equities-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-struggle-against-backdrop-of-sluggish-global-equities-2018-11-05)closed lower, as investors focused on the effects of global trade tensions.
Oil futures ended Monday lower even as sanctions against Iran took effect (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-bounce-around-as-iran-sanctions-kick-in-2018-11-05). The dollar fell 0.3% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/brexit-deal-talk-sends-pound-climbing-against-dollar-2018-11-05) while gold prices were flat.
